summary: In military space developments, the U.S. Senate confirmed Gen. Schiess as the new Chief of Space Operations to lead the Space Force, alongside confirming new leadership for Pentagon space acquisition and the National Reconnaissance Office. Internationally, the European Union expanded the budget and scope of its planned IRIS² satellite constellation to $18 billion, with a Spanish firm taking a key role. In civil space news, NASA secured another year of operations for the 48-year-old Voyager 2 probe, while Northrop Grumman and the Canadian Space Agency announced plans to repurpose their contributions to the Lunar Gateway program. Commercial sector highlights include SpaceX successfully placing 24 Starlink satellites into orbit from California and Redwire booking the first dedicated mission for its Starfall platform, even as engineers work to recover the stricken LINK rescue spacecraft. In planetary science, researchers uncovered daily variations in Uranus's bow shock caused by its unusual rotation, while astronomers continue analyzing early-galaxy observations from the James Webb Space Telescope. Looking ahead, readers should monitor Chinese commercial launcher Landspace as it targets Aug. 10 for a historic rocket launch and recovery attempt.
